title: How do you build a training matrix for a hospitality venue?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a hospitality venue
description: Build a training matrix for a licensed venue: bar, gaming, security, kitchen and duty manager roles against liquor, gambling, AML and guest safety rules.
shortAnswer: A hospitality venue training matrix lists every guest facing and back of house role (bar, floor, gaming, cage, door security, kitchen, duty manager, licensee) against the license conditions and statutes for each venue's market, covering alcohol service, gambling, anti-money laundering, food safety, security licensing, first aid and guest harassment. Each cell records the credential, its expiry, the venue level coverage rule and the document an inspector expects on site.
keyTakeaways: Most venue obligations attach to a personal credential with a fixed life: five years for NSW RSA and RCG endorsements, three years for a Victorian RSA certificate, five years for an NSW food safety supervisor certificate.

Some rules are about coverage, not individuals: NSW hotels and clubs with more than 20 gaming machine entitlements must have one to three Responsible Gambling Officers on duty, depending on entitlements.
Gaming turns a venue into an AML reporting entity: in Australia above 15 gaming machines, and in the United States for casinos and card clubs above $1 million in gross annual gaming revenue.
Inspectors check documents at the venue: Victorian licensees must keep each staff member's current RSA certificate on site, and NSW workers must carry their competency card when working.
Several venue rules changed in 2025 and 2026, including Victorian security license renewal training from 5 October 2026 and Japan's customer harassment duty from October 1, 2026.

sections.heading: What makes a licensed venue's matrix different from other workplaces?

blocks.text: A licensed venue's matrix is driven by the license itself: liquor, gaming and food authorities attach conditions to the premises, and those conditions require named credentials before a person may serve, supervise a gaming room or stand on the door. Missing a credential is not a training gap discovered at audit; it is an offense on the night, often with an on the spot penalty for both the worker and the licensee.

The general approach in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) applies, but three features are specific to hospitality. First, casual and seasonal staff turn over quickly, so a new starter's first shift is the critical date. Second, one person often works across bar, gaming and floor in the same week, so the matrix must follow the shifts a person can be rostered to, not just their job title. Third, some cells are venue level: a room needs a qualified supervisor or gambling officer present whenever it trades. The food side of a venue is covered in more depth in the [food business training matrix guide](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-food-business); this guide concentrates on the licensed floor.

sections.heading: Which venue roles should have their own rows?

blocks.text: Split rows by the activities the license regulates: supplying alcohol, working in a gaming area, handling cash and payouts, monitoring patrons, preparing food and holding the license. A bartender who also patrols the gaming room carries both sets of rows.

sections.heading: Which obligations apply to venues in each market?

blocks.text: Take the columns from the regulation pages for each market where a venue trades. The summaries below are drawn only from those pages.

items: **Australia: alcohol.** In NSW, anyone who sells, serves or supplies alcohol, plus security staff and crowd controllers monitoring patrons, needs RSA from a Liquor & Gaming NSW approved provider; completion gives a 90 day interim certificate and then a competency card valid for five years ([NSW RSA](/regulations/responsible-service-of-alcohol-training-nsw)). In Victoria, staff at general, on-premises, late night and packaged liquor venues need a Certificate of Completion before or within one month of first supplying alcohol, current for three years ([Victorian RSA](/regulations/responsible-service-of-alcohol-training-victoria)).

**Australia: gambling.** NSW requires RCG for staff who patrol or serve in a gaming machine area, and Advanced RCG for Responsible Gambling Officers, licensees, approved managers, club secretaries and gaming supervisors ([NSW RCG](/regulations/nsw-responsible-conduct-of-gambling-training)). Hotels and clubs whose group entitlement exceeds 15 gaming machines, and all casinos, must train personnel under section 26F(4)(e) of the AML/CTF Act and section 5-9 of the AML/CTF Rules 2025 ([AUSTRAC gambling sector](/regulations/austrac-gambling-sector-aml-training)).

**Australia: food, security and first aid.** Standard 3.2.2A requires handler training before a prescribed activity and a food safety supervisor certified within the previous five years ([Standard 3.2.2A](/regulations/food-safety-standard-3-2-2a-training)); NSW requires one supervisor per premises who cannot cover another premises ([NSW FSS](/regulations/nsw-food-safety-supervisor-requirements)), and Queensland licensees must have a supervisor within 30 days of licensing ([Queensland FSS](/regulations/queensland-food-safety-supervisor-requirements)). NSW Class 1A security officers need the NSW Security Licence Course and HLTAID011 first aid issued within three years ([NSW security](/regulations/nsw-security-licence-training-requirements)); Victorian crowd controllers need CPP20218 and, from 5 October 2026, a refresher before renewal ([Victorian security](/regulations/victoria-private-security-licence-training)). The first aid Code recommends annual CPR refreshers and requalification every three years ([first aid](/regulations/first-aid-training-requirements-australia)).

**United States.** FDA Food Code section 2-102.12 says the person in charge shall be a certified food protection manager, but it binds a venue only where the state or local authority has adopted it ([Food Code CFPM](/regulations/fda-food-code-certified-food-protection-manager)). Casinos and card clubs above $1 million in gross annual gaming revenue must train personnel, including in identifying unusual or suspicious transactions, under 31 CFR 1021.210(b)(2)(iii) ([US casino AML](/regulations/casino-aml-training-requirements-us)). California security guards need 8 hours of Power to Arrest and Appropriate Use of Force training before registration and 8 hours of continuing training every year ([California guards](/regulations/california-security-guard-training-requirements)).

**European Union and Portugal.** Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, Annex II, Chapter XII requires food handlers to be supervised and instructed or trained commensurate with their work, with no fixed hours or interval; the European Commission's guidance contrasts the needs of a waiter and a cook ([EU food hygiene](/regulations/eu-food-hygiene-training-requirements)).

**Japan.** Restaurants must appoint a food hygiene manager under Appended Table 17 of the Food Sanitation Act Enforcement Regulation and periodically verify that food handler education works ([Japan food sanitation](/regulations/japan-food-sanitation-act-haccp-and-food-hygiene-manager)). From October 1, 2026, every employer must take measures against customer harassment, with training named as an accepted means ([Japan customer harassment](/regulations/japan-customer-harassment-prevention-obligations)).

sections.heading: How do you handle rules that require someone on duty rather than everyone trained?

blocks.text: Model them as venue rows checked against the roster, because the obligation is met only when a qualified person is present or reachable at the right time. A venue can have every staff member certified and still breach a coverage rule on a night when the rostered supervisor calls in sick.

items: **Responsible Gambling Officers.** NSW hotels and clubs with 21 to 99 gaming machine entitlements need one RGO, 100 to 299 need two and 300 or more need three, with nominated RGOs from midnight to 8am. Liquor & Gaming NSW does not recommend security officers as RGOs.

**Food safety supervisors.** Standard 3.2.2A requires a supervisor who is reasonably available; FSANZ describes that as on site or easily contactable. In NSW, one supervisor cannot cover a second premises.

**Person in charge.** FDA Food Code section 2-101.11 requires a person in charge to be present during all hours of operation, and section 2-102.12 makes that person a certified food protection manager where the code is adopted.

**First aiders.** The model Code recommends one first aider per 50 workers in low risk workplaces and one per 25 in high risk workplaces; Victoria's compliance code uses its own ratios and requires at least one officer available during operating times.
**Security sign-on.** NSW requires sign-on registers each shift, so the register is the evidence that a licensed operative was on the door.

sections.heading: How should a venue track credential expiry and grace periods?

blocks.text: Record the issue date, the expiry rule and any grace period exactly as the regulator states it, because they differ across credentials and a single annual reminder will be wrong for most of them. Venue credentials also behave differently once they lapse.

blocks.text: Where a rule sets no interval, the venue chooses one and records why. FSANZ has set no refresher period for food handler training and calls regular refreshers best practice; Regulation 852/2004 leaves frequency to the needs of the establishment. The guide on [setting mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) covers how to justify the choice.

sections.heading: What will liquor, gaming and food inspectors ask to see?

blocks.text: They ask for the credential itself, at the venue, at the time of inspection. Hospitality evidence is checked in person far more often than in most sectors, so the matrix should show where each document physically sits.

items: **Certificates on site.** Victorian licensees must keep a copy of each staff member's current RSA certificate at the venue and produce it immediately to a liquor inspector or Victoria Police; failure to keep or produce certificates carries a maximum penalty of $1,046. NSW requires a copy of the food safety supervisor certificate on the premises.

**Cards carried.** NSW workers must have their competency card available, physically or digitally, whenever they are in a role that requires it. A worker without a current RSA endorsement faces a $220 penalty notice ($440 in a prescribed precinct), and a licensee who permits it faces $1,100.

**AML training that fits the venue.** AUSTRAC criticizes third party training that does not cover industry money laundering risks or the entity's own program, and says e-learning can't be relied on solely. Its pubs and clubs indicators, such as abandoning a machine above the cheque or EFT threshold or buying TITO tickets, make good assessment scenarios.

**Retention.** California training providers keep guard certificates and exam answer sheets for at least two years; employers keep guard training records for the length of employment. US casinos retain suspicious activity reports and supporting documents for five years.

**Food records.** Category one businesses under Standard 3.2.2A must keep records substantiating critical controls for 3 months. See [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) for record design.

sections.heading: Which venue rules changed recently or are pending?

blocks.text: Several venue obligations changed in 2025 and 2026, and one US casino rule is pending, as at November 2026. Add each as a dated row so affected cells switch on the right day.

items: **30 June 2025, NSW:** RCG became mandatory for club directors (unless they completed Responsible Gambling Board Oversight training) and operational directors of hotel owning companies.
**19 June 2025, Victoria:** every private security activity became a licensed activity under the Private Security and County Court Amendment Act 2024.
**September 17, 2026, United States:** FDA released the 2026 Food Code, adding food defense to the person in charge knowledge areas and to staff training duties; it applies only once adopted locally.
**October 1, 2026, Japan:** customer harassment measures became mandatory for all employers, with ten required measures set by MHLW Notice No. 51 of 2026.

**5 October 2026, Victoria:** renewing security operators need HLTAID011 first aid completed in the three years before expiry, and crowd controllers, guards and bodyguards need an approved refresher in the 12 months before renewal.

blocks.title: Pending, not yet law
blocks.text: FinCEN proposed on April 10, 2026 to replace the casino training wording with the statute's ongoing employee training program language. Comments closed June 9, 2026 and no final rule had been published as at November 2026. Track it as a watch item.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each venue obligation against its source rule, market, credential clock and coverage rule, so a matrix row shows both who must be trained and when a qualified person must be on duty. When a rule such as the Victorian security renewal requirement changes, affected roles and evidence rules are flagged. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Do security staff at an NSW venue need RSA as well as a security license?
faqs.a: Yes. Liquor & Gaming NSW lists security staff and crowd controllers monitoring patron behavior among those who must complete RSA, and the Liquor Regulation 2018 sets a separate penalty notice for crowd controllers without the endorsement. Record both the Class 1A license and the RSA endorsement on the same row.

faqs.q: Does a small pub with a few gaming machines need an AML training program?
faqs.a: Not in Australia if the venue and its related entities are entitled to operate no more than 15 gaming machines. Section 233K exempts them from the AML/CTF program obligations, including training, but not from suspicious matter reporting, so staff still need to know when and how to escalate a suspicion.

faqs.q: Can one RSA course cover staff in NSW and Victoria?
faqs.a: No. Both courses include the national unit SITHFAB021, but each state adds its own content and approves its own providers. A Victorian certificate is current for three years and an NSW card for five, so a worker moving between venues needs both recorded with separate expiry dates.

faqs.q: Is a food safety course enough for a venue's kitchen in every market?
faqs.a: It depends on the market. Australia's Standard 3.2.2A names the topics a handler course must cover, the EU sets no formal course requirement, the FDA Food Code focuses on certifying the person in charge, and Japan requires a food hygiene manager. Record the rule that applies at each venue rather than one generic course.
